transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

I'm seeking help because I've been feeling deeply depressed and constantly exhausted for about a year now. I've lost interest in almost everything I used to enjoy, and even getting through the day feels incredibly heavy. I just really need some help figuring out how to get through this.

Over this past year, have you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day, or have there been stretches of 2 months or more when you felt mostly okay? Did this start after a specific stressful event or major life change?

I've been struggling with low energy and constant fatigue for about a year now, but I haven't really kept track of whether there were clear two-month stretches of feeling completely okay. I'm also not sure if there was a specific stressful event that triggered it; it just seems to have taken over.

During this past year, have you also been worrying excessively about many different things on most days, and is that worry hard to control? Or is the main problem feeling depressed and losing interest in things?

The main problem is definitely feeling depressed, losing interest in everything I used to enjoy, and having no motivation. I don't really experience excessive or uncontrollable worrying about different things. Instead, it's just this deep sense of flatness, fatigue, and loss of interest that has taken over.
In the past 2 years, was there ever a period of 2 months or longer when you were not feeling depressed or low most days? Or has this low mood been pretty continuous without a break that long?

Yes, before this year-long depression started, there was a period of about three months where I didn't feel low at all. Instead, I felt extremely energized, elevated, and on top of the world. It was a complete shift from how I feel now.
During that period when you felt extremely energized and elevated, did you have experiences like hearing or seeing things others didn’t, or strongly believing things that others said weren’t true?
No, I never experienced anything like that. I didn't hear or see things that weren't there, nor did I hold any unusual or false beliefs. I just felt incredibly energized and on top of the world.

During that energized period, did your symptoms become severe enough that you were hospitalized, unable to function normally, or got you into serious trouble at work, financially, or socially? Did it last at least a full week?

Yes, it actually lasted much longer than a week, going on for about three months. While I was incredibly active and energetic during that time, it didn't cause any catastrophic trouble in my life or lead to hospitalization.
During those 3 months, did you also need much less sleep, talk much more than usual, have racing thoughts, feel unusually distractible, or do risky things like overspending or impulsive sex?
No, I didn't really experience any of those things. I slept fine, my thoughts weren't racing, and I didn't do anything reckless or risky. I was just extremely active and had a lot of energy.

During this year of depression, have you also had changes in sleep or appetite, trouble concentrating, feelings of worthlessness or guilt, slowed down or restless movements, or thoughts of death or suicide?

I haven't really had changes in my sleep, appetite, or feelings of guilt, but my concentration is so shot that I can't even focus on TV or conversations. More than that, I've been overwhelmed by constant thoughts of death and suicide, including sudden impulses and actual planning or attempts to end it. It's just exhausting to deal with.

During that 3-month period of feeling energized and elevated, did other people notice you were acting unusually different from your normal self, or did your increased energy mainly just feel like you were doing better than usual?
I definitely felt highly energized and active during those three months. However, I'm not really sure if other people noticed it as unusual, or if they just thought I was doing really well.
During that high-energy period, were you taking on far more activities or goals than usual in a way that was clearly out of character for you, even if it didn’t cause major problems?

Yes, I definitely did. During those three months, I felt like I had endless energy and took on way more work than usual. I ended up starting multiple projects and activities all at the same time because I just couldn't stop moving.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a current major depressive episode with depressed mood, anhedonia, poor concentration, fatigue, and suicidality lasting about a year, plus a distinct prior 3-month period of abnormally elevated/energized mood with increased goal-directed activity. The presence of a sustained manic-spectrum episode rules out Major Depressive Disorder and supports Bipolar I Disorder, even though some classic manic symptoms were denied.
